identifier: compounds according to the invention of the general formula (I)
notes: Markush pointer to the patent's general formula (I), named only by the Tabelle 3 caption, which fixes R2 = Cl, R3 = SO2Et, R4 = H, R5 = H, R6 = OH, Y = CH2, Z = CH2, v = 1, w = 0. Formula (I) is defined elsewhere in the document, so it stays unresolved here. The rows Nr. 390 to 435 assign L and R1. Rows 390, 391, 392 and 393 print 1H NMR (CDCl3) data in the Physikalische Daten column and are recorded separately as compounds; every other row's data cell is empty, so those rows are prophetic enumerations and yield no record. The R1 cells of rows 412, 413, 421, 422, 430 and 431 are drawn structures with no text, and every IMAGE_EXTRACT span in this section returned an empty molecules array, so those substituents are unread.

The compound is defined by the Tabelle 3 caption plus row Nr. 390: the caption fixes R2 = Cl, R3 = SO2Et, R4 = H, R5 = H, R6 = OH, Y = CH2, Z = CH2, v = 1, w = 0, and the row gives L = CH2 and R1 = OCH2CHF2. The name is constructed from those assignments; the row itself prints no name. The row's Physikalische Daten cell carries a 1H NMR block, so this is an entry the patent made and characterised rather than a prophetic enumeration. The scaffold drawing under the caption is an IMAGE_EXTRACT span with an empty molecules array, so the drawn structure was not machine-read and the name rests on the caption text alone. This row prints its ethyl quartet at 3.98 where rows 391 to 393 print theirs between 3.35 and 3.45; reproduced as printed and not corrected.
